 Ho Chi Minh City, southern Vietnam face evening thunderstorms until November 7
 Copy link 
 01/11/2026   10:32 (GMT+07:00) 
 Ho Chi Minh City and southern Vietnam are forecast to experience repeated afternoon and evening thunderstorms over the coming week, before rainfall eases from November 8 and stronger midday sunshine returns.
 According to the Forecasting Department of the Southern Regional Hydro-Meteorological Center, persistent upper-level easterly wind disturbances will continue to affect southern Vietnam over the next week, bringing generally sunny conditions during the day followed by afternoon and evening thunderstorms.
 Scattered thunderstorms concentrated in the afternoon and evening 
 Ho Chi Minh City and southern Vietnam are expected to experience repeated afternoon and evening thunderstorms over the coming week, raising concerns about localised flooding. Photo: Phuoc Sang 
 On November 1, most southern provinces and cities are expected to experience sunshine during the morning and midday, with maximum temperatures generally ranging from 30 to 33 degrees Celsius. Some locations in the southeastern region could see temperatures exceed 33 degrees.
 Along the eastern coastal belt stretching from Ho Chi Minh City to Ca Mau, isolated showers may develop as early as midday.
 Elsewhere, scattered showers and thunderstorms are expected mainly during the afternoon and evening.
 Meteorologists said rainfall in the southeastern region would be concentrated in Lam Dong, northern Dong Nai, Tay Ninh and Ho Chi Minh City.
 In the Mekong Delta, An Giang and Ca Mau are expected to see the heaviest rainfall, with some locations experiencing moderate to heavy showers.
 Rainfall to ease from November 8, intense midday sunshine expected 
 The Southern Regional Hydro-Meteorological Center forecasts that the pattern of intermittent daytime sunshine followed by afternoon and evening thunderstorms will persist across Ho Chi Minh City and southern Vietnam through November 7.
 From November 8, thunderstorms are expected to decrease significantly in both coverage and intensity across the region.
 As rainfall subsides, sunshine is likely to become more intense during the day.
 Residents are advised to take precautions against strong midday sunshine, particularly when travelling or participating in outdoor activities, to protect their health.
